title: Flexible neural population dynamics govern the speed and stability of sensory encoding in mouse visual cortex
goal: Surpass the source-paper result on the same task: Decode one of six visual speeds from V1 activity within each behavioral state; retain within-time accuracy and the original cross-time generalization endpoints.
primary_outputs: Candidate method and outputs for the source task: Decode one of six visual speeds from V1 activity within each behavioral state; retain within-time accuracy and the original cross-time generalization endpoints.

Source-paper comparison for Original state-specific six-class accuracy and Figure 4 cross-time generalization: Accuracy = correct predictions / test trials; chance is 1/6. Equation 21 separately normalizes cross-time accuracy above chance by within-time accuracy above chance.
success_criteria: Recover the exact figure-producing MATLAB settings, original partitions and full accuracy matrices, preserving the distinct within-time and cross-time source protocols.
Compare source-author LDA and candidate on the same five-mouse, state-specific, six-speed task with unchanged features and trial support.
Retain both within-time and cross-time endpoints; a favorable time cell or smaller neuron subset is insufficient.
The pooled-state chronological calibration extension and its local LDA baselines cannot claim a source-paper win.
Freeze candidate method, meaningful effect, paired uncertainty and concrete budgets before final source-task evaluation.
Preserve original cross-time and within-time scores; increasing the relative-performance ratio by degrading its within-time denominator is not scientific improvement.
The bound improvement contract must be improvement_ready and its complete same-task comparison and admission requirements must pass.
Reproduction is calibration only; reconstructing a numerical result, changing the task or split, or achieving stronger significance alone is not success.
